correctness.finding: PASS. The key structural argument is sound. By the published Świątkowski-complex model, the minimal theta graph has only two vertex factors, and each local factor contains at most one homological-degree-1 half-edge generator. Hence the chain complex has C_i=0 for i>=3 in every particle weight. Therefore H_2=ker(d_2) is a subgroup of the free abelian group C_2 and is free abelian. Subdivision does not change the underlying topological graph or its configuration spaces. I also checked the archived exact matrices/log: at k=4 the ranks give H=(1,3,1), and at k=5 H=(1,3,3), matching the published field Betti-number formula for Theta_3.

originality.finding: SUPPORTED, NARROW. An--Drummond-Cole--Knudsen supplies the chain model and a field-valued Betti formula for theta graphs, while An--Knudsen studies generators for H_2 of planar graph braid groups. I did not locate a source stating this exact all-k integral torsion-freeness corollary for Theta_3. The novelty is therefore only the explicit integral corollary/falsification extracted from standard machinery, not a new configuration-space model.

scientific_value.finding: MEANINGFUL TARGET-FALSIFICATION VALUE. The observation definitively rules out the proposed persistent Z/2 class at k=5 and, more strongly, at every weight for the theta graph. It is elementary once the chain model is invoked, so its value is diagnostic and clarifying rather than a major new theorem.

limitations: The result is for H_2 of unordered configurations of the theta graph; it does not address ordered configurations, higher-degree torsion, or graphs with more essential vertices.
The published chain-model theorem is used as an external input, though its consequence C_3=0 => H_2 free is independently checked.
